metadata.title: OSIRIS v5.3.0: Dual-Component Quantum Control Resolution & Empirical Frontier Validation (Experiments E3–E4, ZZ-Ramsey Alias Resolution, and Reproducibility Archive)
metadata.description: Evidence package and clean-room reproducibility foundation for OSIRIS v5.3.0. Contains the definitive empirical resolution of multi-qubit dynamical decoupling (DD) on heavy-hex fixed-frequency transmon processors. Incorporates the complete empirical findings from Experiment E3 on ibm_fez (81 circuits, falsifying single-parameter dephasing portability), the harmonic alias resolution of conditional Hamiltonian ZZ-Ramsey characterizations on ibm_marrakesh (extracting true static coupling zeta_14_15 = 3.170 kHz vs zeta_61_62 = 0.290 kHz), and prospective mechanism-discrimination Experiment E4 (Job dbm9ctu74qds73drs9j0, 72 ISA circuits, 73,728 shots on ibm_marrakesh). The empirical data decisively falsifies pure Microwave Pulse Collision Avoidance (MPCA accounts for only 9.5% of fidelity recovery at boundary contact Delta = 32 ns) and confirms the Dual-Component Model (high-frequency pulse collision contributes <= 10%, while macroscopic timing offsets Delta = 160 ns act as a phase-conjugate cancellation knob against coherent static Hamiltonian crosstalk). Includes the formal peer-review manuscript draft targeting Physical Review Letters, the 180-Day Research-to-Evidence Roadmap, and benchmarks. All code executions and hardware data are anchored by an unbroken 24-block SQLite cryptographic authority chain under SYS-021.
